verses.1: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his steadfast love is eternal.
verses.2: Let those who are rescued by the LORD say, who he has redeemed from the hand of the enemy.
verses.3: From the lands he gathered them, from east and west, from north and sea.
verses.4: They wandered in the desert, in a dry place. They did not find a path to a city, a place to dwell.
verses.5: Hungry and thirsty, their life within them gave out.
verses.6: And they cried out to the LORD in their distress, and he rescued them from their afflictions.
verses.7: And he guided them along a straight path to walk to a city, a place to dwell.
verses.8: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his steadfast love, and his wondrous deeds to the children of humanity.
verses.9: For he filled the soul that was empty, and the soul that was hungry he filled with good.
verses.10: Dwellers in darkness and shadow of death, prisoners in affliction and in iron.
verses.11: For they had scorned the words of God, and the counsel of the Most High they had rejected.
verses.12: And their heart was humbled in toil, they stumbled and had no strength.
verses.13: And they cried out to the LORD in their distress, and he rescued them from their afflictions.
verses.14: He brought them out from darkness and shadow of death, and he broke their chains.
verses.15: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his steadfast love, and his wondrous deeds to the children of humanity.
verses.16: For he broke the bars of bronze, and the iron bolts he shattered.
verses.17: Fools turned aside from their way, and because of their iniquities they were afflicted.
verses.18: Every food their soul despised, and they came near to the gates of death.
verses.19: And they cried out to the LORD in their distress, and he rescued them from their afflictions.
verses.20: He sent his word and healed them, and he rescued them from their destruction.
verses.21: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his steadfast love, and his wondrous deeds to the children of humanity.
verses.22: And let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving, and declare his works with song.
verses.23: Those who go down to the sea in ships, doing labor in the great waters.
verses.24: They saw the works of the LORD and his wondrous deeds in the deep.
verses.25: He spoke, and he raised a stormy wind, and the waves of it were lifted up.
verses.26: They rose to the heavens, they fell to the depths. Their life was in danger, their soul was tossed.
verses.27: They were tossed about, they swayed like a drunkard, and all their wisdom was wasted.
verses.28: And they cried out to the LORD in their distress, and he rescued them from their afflictions.
verses.29: He made the storm cease, and the waves of the sea were hushed.
verses.30: And they rejoiced because they were quieted. He brought them to the harbor of their desire.
verses.31: Let them give thanks to the LORD for his steadfast love, and his wondrous deeds to the children of humanity.
verses.32: And let them exalt him in the assembly of people, and in the gathering of elders let them praise him.
verses.33: He made rivers into a desert, and the outlets of water into a dry land.
verses.34: A fruitful land into a salt waste, because of the wickedness of those who dwelled there.
verses.35: He made a desert into a pool of water, and a dry land into springs of water.
verses.36: And he placed there hungry ones, and they built a city to dwell in.
verses.37: And they sowed fields, and planted vineyards, and made fruit for their harvest.
verses.38: And he blessed them, and they multiplied greatly, and their livestock did not diminish.
verses.39: And they were diminished and afflicted, through the oppression of wickedness and sorrow.
verses.40: He cast a curse on the nobles, and led them astray in a barren way, without a path.
verses.41: And he rescued the poor from affliction, and made their families as flocks.
verses.42: The upright will see and rejoice, and all iniquity will shut its mouth.
verses.43: Who is the wise and will keep these things, and understand the steadfast love of the LORD?

notes:
Notes
- v. 40: "He cast a curse on the nobles" reflects the poetic inversion of justice, where the mighty suffer due to their wrongdoing.
- v. 43: "Who is the wise and will keep these things" — the rhetorical question invites reflection on the lessons of divine steadfast love and human need for gratitude and humility.
